findings.text: Two public operations remove memory, one taking a start address plus length and another taking an array of ranges with a count. Both require block sized alignment and non empty input, report invalid input and allocation failure with negative codes, and return success only after all blocks are offlined and removed.

Range removal behaves as a two outcome transaction under hotplug exclusion. Offlining covers every block while remembering each prior online mode with untouched entries marked offline. Any offline failure triggers a compensating pass that restores only touched blocks, while total success proceeds to removal which is expected to succeed.

Per block offlining infers a kernel or movable mode from the resident page zone, attempts device transition, records the inferred mode solely on success, always advances the tracking cursor, and treats already offline as success. The companion reonline pass skips untouched entries, reinstalls the remembered mode before device transition, warns on failure, advances the cursor, and always reports continuation.

Range removal serializes against concurrent hotplug activity by holding the device hotplug lock from the beginning of the offline sweep through completion of removal and rollback, releasing it before freeing tracking storage and returning.

Mempool lifecycle comprises initialization of a caller supplied object, node aware creation that allocates the descriptor, teardown that drains reserve and releases array storage, destruction tolerant of null, and resizing to a new guaranteed minimum.

Initialization establishes spin state and wait queue, records callbacks and opaque data and minimum, ensures array capacity for at least one slot even when minimum is zero, pre fills reserve up to the guaranteed level using caller flags, and on any creation failure releases partial state and reports resource exhaustion.

Resizing to a smaller guarantee discards surplus reserve outside the lock and then updates the minimum under protection. Resizing upward allocates a larger array, abandons the attempt if a concurrent resize already satisfied the request, otherwise installs the new array, raises the minimum, and fills toward it, freeing any surplus element produced by a race. Caller context may sleep.

Allocation services include single element allocation with caller reclaim flags, bulk allocation of a caller array with kernel reclaim semantics, nonblocking consumption of reserve, bulk return reporting how many entries were absorbed, single return that forwards overflow to the backing releaser, plus paired helpers for slab caches, sized heap blocks, and paged extents.

Single and bulk allocation first attempt fresh creation with allocation constrained to avoid rescue memory, retry and warnings and with reclaim and IO privileges withheld initially, then consume reserve, then retry creation with fuller caller privileges. Fault injection can force the reserve path for stress, with bulk injection affecting the whole request. Bulk requests larger than the guarantee and single requests asking for cleared memory are flagged as suspicious.

Reserve consumption succeeds only when enough entries are present, otherwise it either sleeps briefly outside the lock awaiting a return when the caller permits reclaim, waking periodically to retest fresh creation, or returns immediately without sleeping. Successful bulk consumption refreshes leak tracking for returned entries and orders visibility for concurrent frees.

Returning storage refills reserve only while occupancy is below guarantee, using an unlocked test for promptness followed by a locked refill, with a dedicated path ensuring progress when both guarantee and occupancy are zero. A return that added entries wakes sleepers only if sleepers exist. Ordering is enforced so a free observes occupancy from after the corresponding allocation even when the pointer was handed off without barriers.

When debug is enabled and sanitizer is inactive, reserve pushes apply a fill pattern with a distinct terminator and reserve pops validate the pattern over the object extent appropriate to the backing type, using cache object size for slab, byte size for heap, and page extent for paged backing with per page temporary mapping on high memory systems. Mismatch produces diagnostic output and a stack trace. Sanitizer poisoning and unpoisoning are applied symmetrically on push and pop according to backing type.

A per pool spin lock with interrupt state preservation guards occupancy, guarantee and array slots during push, pop, shrink, grow and refill. The lock is not held across backing creation, backing release, or timed waiting. Bulk allocation and freeing use paired write and read ordering around the locked sections to coordinate occupancy visibility.

Reserve storage behaves as a stack indexed by current occupancy. Push asserts spare capacity and then stores, pop retrieves then decrements and asserts non negativity. Both apply debug and sanitizer transitions. Teardown repeatedly pops until empty and forwards each entry to the backing releaser before releasing the array and clearing the pointer.

Several misuses are treated as programming errors, including resizing to a non positive guarantee, overflowing or underflowing reserve, supplying a slab cache with a constructor for pooled slab use, requesting cleared memory from the pool, or bulk requesting more than the guarantee. Poison corruption is reported with pool identity, size, occupancy, address window around the fault and a stack trace.

Two early hooks control testing support, a boot string enables pooled object debugging and an early initializer publishes failure injection controls for single and bulk allocation. A separate early parser records the memory init verbosity level.

Global descriptors expose maximum frame number, base of the page array, top of directly mapped memory, zero page frame number and page pointer with post init read only protection, init verbosity level in init data, and the memory subsystem kernel object.

Early verification logs configured widths and shifts for section, node, zone, last CPU, sanitizer tag and generational fields, then derives expected bit positions by subtracting configured widths from word size and asserts agreement with compiled shifts, and finally asserts that combined zone node section masks contain no overlapping bits by comparing OR combination against additive combination.

The opaque pool context changes meaning by backing type, byte length for heap blocks, cache pointer whose usable size is obtained through an object size accessor for slab blocks, and page order integer for paged extents. Allocation and release helpers interpret the same context accordingly and never mix interpretations.

Range removal rejects null descriptors, empty counts, unaligned starts or lengths, zero length, and tracking allocation failure. Already offline blocks do not fail the sweep. Once offlining succeeds for all ranges, removal is treated as infallible under exclusion and any failure is reported through a once only warning.
